subject: info-dy
title: INFO.DY.------C.CONT.
description: Diagram in AF(D)-9 (Affinity Dynamics, Level One), second of two on book p81, paired with v2-p81-1. Continues the same argument: that affinity-dynamics operates as a structural layer beneath race-thinking, and that information-dynamics must be read multidimensionally. INFO-DY (information dynamics) is crossed with C-CONT (composite continuance): the question is what information-dynamics produces when crossed with composite-continuance — given that 'every projectional thrust of knowledge must take into account its affinity dynamics.' C-CONT sits at the top with MT-INFO (multi-information) on the upper-right output. INFO-PROJ (information projection) anchors the right margin. IST-FT (interior-source fundamentals) feeds into INFO-DY from the left. AF-DY (affinity dynamics) sits between subject and partner as central hub. ALT-C-PG (alternative culture program) anchors the lower-left. SOC-RT-INT (social-reality interior) feeds upward into AF-DY from below. (P)STF (point-of-activation source-transfer-functionalism) hangs on the right via a *dashed* edge — the only conditional relation in the diagram, marking that source-transfer-functionalism is here functioning at a *trigger* level rather than as sustained operation. PROG-EXT-F (progressional extended functionalism) anchors the lower-right via the dashed line from (P)STF. Structural argument: information-dynamics crossed with composite-continuance is mediated by affinity-dynamics as the central hub — the same hub as in v2-p81-1, registering Braxton's structural commitment that affinity-dynamics is *the* organizing layer. The (p) prefix and dashed edge on STF together expose that source-transfer becomes operative as a trigger, not a sustained drive, and the consequent route to progressional-extended-functionalism is conditional rather than guaranteed.
